chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Khalid, from Muhammad bin Ali al-Kufi, from Ahmad bin Muhammad al-Bazanti, that he said: Abu’l-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: The Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) said:

None rejects generosity except for a donkey. I said: And what is the meaning of that? So he said: That is with regards to the one to whom perfume is presented, and (to whom it is offered) a wide sitting place. The one who rejects them, is as he said.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the saying 'None rejects generosity except for a donkey'?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates Imam Ali’s metaphor by linking the 'donkey' to one who rejects material honors like perfume and spacious seating, which are considered forms of *karah* (generosity/honor) in the cultural context of the time. This interpretation highlights that rejecting such tangible signs of respect is a sign of lowliness, contrasting with the noble disposition of accepting the good things of life as a right. The saying thus serves as a practical guide for social etiquette, emphasizing that humility should not be confused with the rejection of legitimate honor.
